---
title: Declare, then assemble
description: "Why an Arkitekt app is a declaration that does no I/O, how it is assembled into a manifest only when it is run or inspected, and how the same declaration is served by different runtimes."
type: concept
---

An Arkitekt app is a **declaration**: a description of who it is and what it offers. Writing it
does nothing. No connection opens, nothing is registered, nothing is checked yet. Only when the app
is **run, inspected or checked** is the declaration assembled into what the platform needs: a
manifest, the ports of every action, the clients it uses, the requirements it has.

```python
from arkitekt import App
from mikro.arkitekt.specs import Volume

app = App("denoise", "0.1.0")          # records who the app is


@app.action                            # records one more thing it offers
def denoise(volume: Volume, sigma: float = 1.5) -> Volume:
    """Denoise"""
    ...
```

Importing this module has no effect beyond building two Python objects. `arkitekt check` assembles
it and reports every problem at once, each at its line. `arkitekt inspect all` prints the manifest
it would register. `run(app)` assembles it and then connects.

## The pattern

This is the split between **description and execution** found in build systems, infrastructure as
code and dependency injection containers: you describe the desired result, and a separate step
turns the description into action. In Arkitekt that step is *assembly*, and the same declaration
can be assembled many times, by different tools, for different purposes.

## What it buys

- **Inspecting without running.** The CLI imports your module to check it, list its actions,
  package it and build its image. None of that needs a server, a GPU or the hardware the app drives.
- **All errors at once.** Because nothing is checked at the decorator, assembly can look at the
  whole app and report every problem together, instead of stopping at the first.
- **No manifest to keep in sync.** The manifest is computed from the code. There is no second file
  that can drift from it.
- **One declaration, several runtimes.** The same app is served by the Rekuest agent
  (`run(app)`), from a FastAPI server (`serve(app, api)`), called in-process in a test, or used
  only for its clients (`connect(app)`). The runtime that serves the offerings is a *provider*
  chosen at run time, in the spirit of ports and adapters: the actions do not know which one runs
  them.

## What it costs

- **Nothing may happen at import.** Opening a device or loading a model at module level runs it
  every time the CLI looks at the app (see [Anti-patterns](/docs/build/anti-patterns#import-time)).
  That work belongs in startup hooks, which run only when the app really runs.
- **Errors come later than the line that caused them.** A wrong annotation is reported when the app
  is assembled, not when the decorator runs. `arkitekt check` closes that gap: run it in CI.
